title: CNN Panelist ROASTS Conservative Over Bizarre Claims LIVE
description:
When a foreign policy deal falls apart just three weeks after it was signed, the fallout tells you everything about how the strategy was built. In this heated CNN panel discussion, the NewsNight roundtable breaks down how a short-lived agreement with Iran collapsed almost overnight, and whether the response that followed represents strategy, improvisation, or something closer to political theater. The conversation is sharp, fast, and deeply divided, and it captures one of the most consequential debates in American foreign policy right now.

The panel digs into the core question: is the United States winning or losing in the standoff over the Straits of Hormuz? On one side, commentators argue that the military campaign devastated Iran's capabilities and that walking away from a bad deal was the right call. On the other, analysts insist the entire approach has been exposed as reactive and improvised, with no clear exit strategy and no long-term plan beyond repeated strikes. The disagreement is real, and both sides bring receipts.

Kian, a longtime regional expert who has advised on how to negotiate with Iran, argues that Washington has fallen into a trap laid for every administration, sending polished diplomats to talk while the hardliners who actually control the ships ignore whatever is said at the table. Max lays out the case that the conflict has hardened into a forever war with no military solution, and that the nuclear program was never fully eradicated despite the public
